title: Service Trust Sprint Orchestra — Implementation Plan
content:
Executive summary:

This implementation plan—Service Trust Sprint Orchestra—lays out an 8-week cross-functional program to standardize SLOs, harden operational handoffs, and embed lightweight telemetry-based experiments across product, platform, and SRE. Goal is to create a repeatable sprint template that feature teams can adopt to move from ad-hoc reliability changes to predictable improvements that surface measurable user impact.

Primary objectives:
- Define and standardize service-level objectives (latency & error SLOs) for three pilot services representing different load profiles (low-latency API, batch embeddings, long-running private deploy jobs).
- Reduce mean P95 latency for the low-latency API by 15% during peak while keeping cost delta <= 5%.
- Introduce a lightweight SLO feedback loop: alerts -> postmortem-lite -> corrective experiment -> metric-based rollback.
- Ship an SLO onboarding checklist and playbook for product teams to follow during feature launches.

Scope and out-of-scope:
- In scope: telemetry schema changes, common SLO definitions, alert routing updates, a canary rollout pattern for SLO experiments, runbook templates, training session for oncall.
- Out of scope: major architecture rewrites, infra procurement decisions, audit/compliance changes to Private deployments (separate workstream).

Stakeholders and roles:
- Executive sponsor: VP Platform (Kendra Brooks) — approves success criteria and funding.
- Program lead: Aisha Patel (platform-engineering) — overall coordination.
- SRE lead: Diego Morales — defines operational guardrails, runbooks, oncall changes.
- Product liaison: Priya Kapoor — product-level priorities and acceptance criteria.
- Applied ML representative: Evan Li — model-serving considerations for embedding workloads.
- Solutions/PS: Marta Nowak — customer impact lens and rollout cadence to Dedicated/Private customers.

Workstreams (parallel):
1) SLO Definition & Cataloging
   - Owner: Product + SRE
   - Deliverables: SLO spec template (latency, availability, user-impact mapping), catalog of pilot services and their baseline measurements, SLO thresholds proposal for review.

2) Observability & Telemetry
   - Owner: Platform infra
   - Deliverables: standardized metric names/labels for service, span + trace tagging guidelines, dashboards (token-level cost / latency breakdown), alert rule templates.

3) Runbooks & Playbooks
   - Owner: SRE
   - Deliverables: incident-to-SLO postmortem-lite template, escalation matrix, rollback criteria, safety-net fallback policy for model variants.

4) Canary & Experimentation Pattern
   - Owner: Platform + Release Eng
   - Deliverables: canary policy for SLO experiments, A/B rollout recipe, automated rollback hook (based on SLO delta and error budget).

5) Training & Onboarding
   - Owner: DevX + Platform
   - Deliverables: 90-minute workshop, slide deck, quickstart checklist, office-hours schedule for first 6 weeks after launch.

Milestones and timeline (8-week sprint orchestra):
- Week 0 (Prep / kickoff): finalize pilot services, baseline metric pull, stakeholder alignment.
- Week 1: SLO workshop — draft SLOs for pilots, agree on user impact mapping.
- Week 2: Implement telemetry changes (labels, traces) for pilot services; dashboard skeletons.
- Week 3: Runbook drafts and alert rules deployed to staging; execute tabletop for one failure mode.
- Week 4: Canary tooling configured; experiment plan for latency-improvement patch; training session #1.
- Week 5: Run controlled canary; monitor SLOs and error budget consumption; collect experiment telemetry.
- Week 6: Postmortem-lite + decision: promote, iterate, or roll back; update runbooks.
- Week 7: Consolidate artifacts into playbook, finalize onboarding checklist, publish dashboards and runbooks.
- Week 8: Program retrospective, acceptance review with VP Platform; handoff to enablement track for broader rollout.

Success criteria (measureable):
- Three pilot SLOs defined and published in the SLO catalog with baseline and target thresholds.
- At least one meaningful reliability improvement (>=10% measured improvement in the chosen metric) validated in production canary.
- Oncall noise reduced: false-positive alert rate for pilot services decreases by 20%.
- Playbook published and used by >=2 feature teams within 30 days.

Risk & mitigation log:
- Risk: Telemetry gaps across services make SLO calculations inaccurate.
  Mitigation: Run an initial 7-day telemetry audit and instrument minimal required labels before Week 2.
- Risk: Experimentation causes customer-visible regressions.
  Mitigation: Strict canary size limits, automatic rollback on SLO breach, and pre-approved fallback variants.
- Risk: Stakeholder bandwidth conflicts slow delivery.
  Mitigation: Timebox decision windows, identify backup approvers, and raise escalations at weekly executive check-ins.

Communications cadence:
- Weekly program sync (30 min) — core leads only (Mon 10am PT).
- Bi-weekly cross-functional demo (30 min) — broader audience + product stakeholders.
- Slack channel: #trust-sprint-orchestra — for async updates; use pinned notes for artifacts and meeting notes.
- Exec checkpoint: every 2 weeks with VP Platform.

Metrics & dashboards to publish:
- SLO compliance: rolling 7d and 30d windows, error budget burn rate.
- Latency distribution: P50/P95/P99 with token-level breakdown for inference paths.
- Alert volume: actionable vs noise ratio.
- Cost delta: incremental GPU/CPU cost per experiment window.

Dependencies and prerequisites:
- Baseline metric export from Prometheus -> Tempo/Tracing available for pilot services.
- Release Eng to provide canary pipeline slot for experiments.
- Product approval on SLO thresholds for customer-impacting endpoints.

Kickoff checklist (must be complete before Week 1):
- Draft SLO template reviewed by SRE and Product.
- Pilot services list finalized and owners assigned.
- Access granted to dashboards and metrics for all core leads.
- Canary pipeline slot reserved and smoke-tests defined.
- Calendar invites and Slack channel created.

Playbook excerpt (quickstart):
1) Pick a pilot endpoint and compute baseline (7–14 days).
2) Map user-facing impact to metric (e.g., token-latency -> perceived typing lag).
3) Propose SLO threshold and expected impact; gather sign-off.
4) Deploy telemetry additions to staging; validate.
5) Run canary with small traffic slice; monitor SLOs and roll back on defined triggers.
6) Conduct postmortem-lite and publish lessons into SLO catalog.

Open questions (for program kickoff):
- Which team owns cross-service SLO enforcement policy (central SRE vs. platform-engineering)?
- What constitutes a "customer-impacting" threshold for Private deployments—must legal/compliance weigh in?
- Is a single alert routing path sufficient for both Hosted API and Dedicated pools, or do we need separate routing rules?

Appendix: pilot services candidates (brief):
- gateway-api (low-latency): user request path, auth + generation critical path.
- embed-batch (throughput): recurring embedding jobs for downstream search.
- private-agent (long-run): customer-managed private deployments with periodic model loads.

Next steps (action items for program lead):
- Send kickoff invite and pre-read (SLO template + baseline exec summary) by EOD Friday.
- Schedule telemetry audit and confirm Prometheus queries by Nov 10.
- Lock pilot owners and confirm canary pipeline window by Nov 12.

Notes to self: keep artifact lightweight; teams adopt faster if runbooks are three pages max. Prioritize experiments that produce clear delta on user-impact metrics.
